 Lakers head coach JJ Redick said ahead of Tuesday’s game against the Hornets that Austin Reaves will get on the court Wednesday to test his injured heel. 
 Tuesday’s game will be the second Reaves has missed since injuring his left heel during a November 11 win over the Bucks. The plan is for him to take the court Wednesday to test his heel and see how he feels. Quentin Grimes should remain in the starting lineup for as long as Reaves is out. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Lakers head coach JJ Redick said Wednesday that Austin Reaves (heel) had a good workout but lacks a return timeline. 
 Wednesday’s game against the Jazz will be the third that Reaves has missed due to a bone bruise in his left heel. While his workout on Wednesday went well, the lack of a return timeline is a concern. Quentin Grimes, who hit 10 three-pointers and scored 47 points in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets, will start until Reaves returns. 
 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Austin Reaves (heel) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Reaves will miss his third game in a row with a heel injury. Quentin Grimes should continue starting in Reaves’ absence and should be rostered in all formats. 
 Quentin Grimes 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets. 
 Grimes had the best game of his career on Tuesday, and the Lakers needed it, trailing by as much as 18 late in the third quarter before rallying to win in overtime. Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter alone, outscoring the Hornets by four, and his three-pointer with 1.7 seconds left forced overtime. Austin Reaves (heel) is supposed to test his injured heel on Wednesday before that night’s game against the Jazz, so we should learn more about how much time he’ll miss. Grimes, the first Laker other than Reaves, Luka Dončić or LeBron James to record a 30-point game since Dalton Knecht did in March 2025, will start as long as Reaves is out, and he’s worth rostering until that changes.

 #15 
 Austin Reaves (heel) has been ruled out for Tuesday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Reaves will remain out for a second game due to this heel injury, and there isn’t a clear timeline as to how long he’ll end up being sidelined. Until he’s back, Quentin Grimes will continue to start, especially after he had 22 points and five triples in 37 minutes on Sunday. 
 Quentin Grimes 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Quentin Grimes tallied 22 points (7-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and five three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Suns. 
 The Lakers played Sunday’s game without Austin Reaves (heel), which led to Grimes moving into the starting lineup. He shot 5-of-6 from beyond the arc, and his 22 points were the most in a game for the Lakers’ wing since October 28 against the Clippers. That game, in which Grimes scored 23 points, was one the Lakers played without Luka Dončić. If available, Grimes should be rostered on any night when the Lakers are without one of their two star guards.

 The Lakers will be without Austin Reaves on Sunday, as he suffered a left heel injury during Wednesday’s win over the Bucks and is day-to-day. Grimes, who missed the last two games with a finger injury, is available and will start. The Lakers’ other four starters are unchanged.

 Austin Reaves 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #15 
 ESPN’s Dave McMenamin reports that Austin Reaves is listed as day-to-day with a bruised heel. 
 According to head coach JJ Redick, Reaves and the Lakers medical staff opted against imaging. This latest update is favorable for the severity of the injury, and Reaves could miss little time, if any at all. If Reaves is forced to sit out, Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes could pick up the slack. 
 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Luka Dončić (ankle) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 32 points (10-of-25 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, three steals and five three-pointers. 
 Dončić has scored at least 30 points in each of his last nine appearances. However, there was a concerning moment when the Lakers star appeared to tweak his ankle during the fourth quarter. The benches were being cleared at this point, so Dončić returned to the Lakers’ locker room with a team trainer with 4:23 remaining in the fourth quarter. We’ll see if he lands on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Spurs, especially with Austin Reaves (heel) leaving Wednesday’s victory during the third quarter.

 Mitchell’s run of excellent play continued against the Bucks Wednesday.  It continues to be the Wagner show for the Magic with Paolo Banchero (hamstring) still sidelined.
